name: Shin-Seibijo
tagline: Tokyo in 41 minutes and Shinagawa in 41 minutes. Served by 1 line.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Tokyo Monorail. Journey times to the main business districts are 46 minutes to Otemachi, 52 minutes to Shinjuku, 47 minutes to Shibuya and 41 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 5.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 8.2 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 5.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.9 m to 9.1 m, a difference of 8.2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Monorail.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Monorail. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

neighbours.lead: For the number of places to eat out, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2; for quiet, Shin-Seibijo.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Seibijo. Both have the Tokyo Monorail. Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 also has the Keikyu Airport Line, which Shin-Seibijo does not. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On quiet, Shin-Seibijo comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Shin-Seibijo is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Shin-Seibijo in a straight line. Both have the Tokyo Monorail. Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 also has the Keikyu Airport Line, which Shin-Seibijo does not. Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 is 7 minutes quicker to Shinagawa, but times to the other main business districts are much the same. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, Shin-Seibijo comes out ahead.
